question: Can a single learned desirability score per item correct errors shared by existing pair classifiers? A strictly shared scorer gives A-vs-B the opposite log odds from B-vs-A and gives transitive score differences.
scope: Use the actual two distinct frozen feature providers elected by previous training feedback and the actual protected four-member probabilities bound in the semantic tree study. This is a research capability test for binary ordered comparisons only. No dataset or encoder name in the scorer.
training: The two comparators get exactly the same 2685 fitting comparisons and one score for each item. For each of the two fitted-text encoder matrices fit a deterministic 64-coordinate PCA and standardize its outputs on fitting texts only; add standardized generic text shape counts. Use a linear utility control, and a separate shared linear utility plus one 32-unit tanh hidden layer. Both optimize binary cross entropy of u(left)-u(right), in identical deterministic batches of 128, 16 epochs with AdamW and no held-set early stopping. Count two PCA fits separately from two supervised fits.
choice: The earlier nomination role was already used to choose feature providers. Lock the fitted heads before using the separate 1318-comparison confirmation role to choose the best of retaining the previous portfolio or adding either scorer at 25%, 50%, or 100%. Break ties in favor of less new weight then simpler head. Open the 1309-row audit role only for a nonzero winning choice. Positive gain there and pooled gain at least 0.20 points are required to warrant ordinary integration. Count recoveries and losses and rows on which all protected members were wrong. This is a reused development panel, not a course grade.
budget: Two small supervised fits, two unsupervised projections, zero additional base fits, zero model API calls. No course-designated validation, official test or H2.
